cmo_output.executive_summary: January 2099 should use 20 English-language Instagram posts to learn which combination of real-life habit pain, concrete adaptive-product evidence, and early-adopter invitation produces attributable landing and activation behavior. The available analytics are historical fallback data rather than evidence from December 2098, and prior campaigns have no measured post results, so the plan preserves the established positioning but treats performance conclusions as unresolved. Execution should prioritize three measurable comparisons, reuse traceable square static and carousel assets, require human review, and keep acquisition, registration, activation, and product usage distinct.

strategic_diagnosis.primary_problem: Innerbloom has a coherent positioning and an operational content pipeline but lacks matched-period, post-attributed evidence showing which message moves a defined audience from Instagram to landing intent and activation.
supporting_problems: The priority audience is inferred rather than researched
The activation funnel is incomplete because auth_completed is missing
Prior approvals are available but performance and decision notes are not
Existing product proof is concentrated in one Daily Quest screenshot
strategic_diagnosis.why_it_matters: Without disciplined attribution and distinct funnel reporting, producing 20 posts would add volume without revealing whether pain, mechanism, or early-adopter participation improves acquisition or activation.
strategic_diagnosis.decision_needed_after_this_period: Decide which pain-to-proof message pair deserves the next period's majority allocation, whether static or carousel is more efficient for attributable landing intent, and whether the early-adopter feedback invitation produces activation signals strong enough to retain.

secondary_objectives: Validate attributable landing intent by message and format
Observe activation progression separately from acquisition

priority_audience.description: Provisional English-speaking Instagram users who want sustainable habits but feel alienated by streak pressure, perfect-day plans, or all-or-nothing restarts.
main_pains: A missed day feels like lost progress
Rigid systems demand the same effort regardless of energy or schedule
main_desires: A habit rhythm that can flex without losing direction
A practical way to return after disruption
objections: This may be generic motivational advice
Adaptive may mean vague or unstructured
An early-stage product may not yet be useful enough
priority_audience.current_awareness_level: Problem-aware and solution-curious; awareness of Innerbloom is not established.

strategy.core_value_proposition: Innerbloom helps people keep direction by adapting habit effort to real life, making recalibration and visible progress more useful than rigid streak perfection.
strategy.period_narrative: A sustainable habit is not one that demands perfect days; it is one that gives you a clear way to adapt, see progress, and return.
strategic_priorities: Turn familiar rigid-habit pain into attributable landing intent
Make the adaptive mechanism concrete with available product evidence
Invite qualified early adopters into a measurable try-and-feedback loop

content_pillars.name: Real-life friction
content_pillars.purpose: Create recognition among people failed by rigid habit systems.
content_pillars.audience_problem: Streaks and fixed plans collapse when energy, stress, or schedules change.
content_pillars.message: The system, not the person, may be mismatched to real life.
content_pillars.proof_or_mechanism: Contrast rigid same-output expectations with the need for adjustable intensity; frame as a problem hypothesis, not a proven universal claim.

content_pillars.name: Adaptive mechanism
content_pillars.purpose: Explain how Innerbloom's adaptive promise becomes concrete.
content_pillars.audience_problem: Adaptive habit language can sound vague without a visible mechanism.
content_pillars.message: Recalibration, task intensity, Daily Quest, dashboard progress, and review can preserve direction through changing days.
content_pillars.proof_or_mechanism: Use only verified product screens and capabilities represented in supplied context or assets; show the Daily Quest screenshot where relevant.

content_pillars.name: Return without shame
content_pillars.purpose: Differentiate Innerbloom from all-or-nothing habit narratives.
content_pillars.audience_problem: Missing a day can trigger guilt and a restart-from-zero response.
content_pillars.message: Returning and recalibrating are part of sustainable consistency; perfection is not the requirement.
content_pillars.proof_or_mechanism: Use conceptual contrasts and visible-progress language without promising outcomes.

content_pillars.name: Early-adopter loop
content_pillars.purpose: Convert qualified curiosity into a try-and-feedback action.
content_pillars.audience_problem: An early product needs a clear reason to try now despite uncertainty.
content_pillars.message: People dissatisfied with rigid habit tools can try the early version and help evaluate whether adaptive habits feel useful.
content_pillars.proof_or_mechanism: Be transparent that the product is early, direct users to the tracked landing path, and ask for feedback only after product exposure.

experiments.name: Pain framing and landing intent
experiments.hypothesis: For the provisional audience, posts framing plans that fail on messy weeks will produce a higher landing_cta_clicked rate per attributable landing session than posts framing broken-streak pressure.
experiments.variable_being_tested: Messy-week planning pain versus broken-streak pressure, holding format, CTA family, publishing window, and destination consistent.
experiments.control_or_baseline: Broken-streak framing is the comparison baseline; no historical winner is assumed.
experiments.target_audience: Problem-aware Instagram users frustrated by rigid habit systems.
experiments.primary_metric: landing_cta_clicked events divided by attributable landing sessions for each message variant
secondary_metrics: auth_started events by variant if attribution is retained
experiments.success_criteria: Select a direction only if each variant has at least 30 attributable landing sessions and one variant's CTA-click rate is at least 25% higher than the other.
experiments.failure_criteria: Neither variant reaches 30 attributable landing sessions, tracking cannot retain variant attribution, or the rate difference is below 25%.
experiments.minimum_evidence_needed: At least two posts per pain frame, matched across one static and one carousel where possible, and 30 attributable landing sessions per variant.
experiments.decision_enabled: Choose the dominant pain frame for the next period or repeat the test unchanged if evidence is insufficient.

experiments.name: Product proof format
experiments.hypothesis: A carousel that connects a real-life problem to a verified product mechanism will produce a higher landing_cta_clicked rate per attributable landing session than a static post using the same mechanism and CTA.
experiments.variable_being_tested: Carousel versus static presentation of the same product mechanism.
experiments.control_or_baseline: Static product-proof post; no historical format winner is assumed.
experiments.target_audience: Solution-curious users who need evidence that adaptive habits are concrete.
experiments.primary_metric: landing_cta_clicked events divided by attributable landing sessions by format
secondary_metrics: Instagram reach and saves if manually imported from Metricool
experiments.success_criteria: Prefer a format only if each cell has at least 30 attributable landing sessions and its CTA-click rate exceeds the other by at least 25%.
experiments.failure_criteria: Insufficient sessions, unequal destination or CTA, missing UTM attribution, or less than 25% rate separation.
experiments.minimum_evidence_needed: At least two matched static/carousel pairs using verified mechanisms and 30 attributable landing sessions per format.
experiments.decision_enabled: Allocate more next-period product-proof posts to the more efficient format, or preserve a balanced mix if inconclusive.

experiments.name: Try versus co-creation invitation
experiments.hypothesis: An explicit early-adopter co-creation invitation will produce a higher auth_started rate per attributable landing session than a generic try-the-product invitation.
experiments.variable_being_tested: Transparent co-creation/feedback CTA versus generic try CTA.
experiments.target_audience: Users who recognize rigid-habit pain and accept an early-stage product.
experiments.primary_metric: auth_started events divided by attributable landing sessions for each CTA variant
secondary_metrics: auth_completed events if tracking is restored
dashboard_view events after auth completion if cohort attribution is available
experiments.success_criteria: Retain the co-creation CTA if each variant reaches at least 30 attributable landing sessions and its auth-start rate is at least 25% higher than control, with no tracking break between landing and auth.
experiments.failure_criteria: Minimum traffic is not reached, auth attribution is unavailable, or co-creation does not exceed control by 25%.
experiments.minimum_evidence_needed: At least two posts per CTA variant and 30 attributable landing sessions per variant; verify auth_started instrumentation before launch.
experiments.decision_enabled: Choose the activation invitation for the next cycle or record the result as inconclusive without claiming a winner.

brand.objective: Acquire early adopter users for Innerbloom 2.0 with lightweight, measurable social content. The system should minimize manual marketing operations while keeping final approval under human control.
positioning: Innerbloom helps people build sustainable habits that adapt to real life instead of forcing rigid streaks or perfect-day productivity.
content_rules: GA4 active users are anonymous, cookie/device-based users. They are not the same as registered users in Neon.
For marketing decisions:
Treat landing page views as acquisition signal.
Treat `/innerbloom2/...` pages as product usage signal.
Exclude auth redirects such as `accounts.google.com`.
Exclude internal/admin emails before reading registered-user growth.
Search Console is sparse until Google has more impressions.
This is the first real monthly plan once draft generation is wired.
Planned mix:
8 pain/friction posts: streak pressure, perfect-day planning, restarting from zero, habits collapsing during messy weeks.
5 product mechanism/demo posts: adaptive rhythm, weekly recalibration, dashboard progress, task intensity, visible momentum.
4 belief/differentiation posts: real weeks over perfect calendars, progress without shame, sustainable habit design, anti-all-or-nothing routines.
3 early-adopter CTA posts: try the early version, help shape the product, give feedback after using the dashboard.
Creative rules:
Prefer real Innerbloom 2.0 screenshots over generic lifestyle imagery.
Use both dark-mode and light-mode product assets when available.
Keep carousel slides readable on mobile.
Use R2 URLs in Metricool CSV output.
Store source assets and planning context in Google Drive for browsing.
Measurement:
Primary acquisition: landing views and CTA events from UTM-tagged links.
Primary activation: `auth_started -> auth_completed -> dashboard_view`.
Product-interest proxy: views of `/innerbloom2/dashboard`, `/innerbloom2/tareas`, `/innerbloom2/task-detail`, and `/innerbloom2/logros`.
For the next monthly run:
Keep the number of configurable knobs small.
Prefer strong hooks and measurable hypotheses over generic motivational posts.
Reuse visual patterns that remain readable on mobile.
Generate only new visuals when the existing asset library cannot support the post.
Preserve every decision and result in this strategy memory.

Instagram posts published successfully from the generated CSV.
Cloudflare R2 is now the publishing asset store for CSV exports.
Google Drive remains the human-readable marketing library.
GA4 and Search Console snapshots can be synced into Neon and shown in `/admin/marketing`.
